ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signature screening and ongoing monitoring against the consolidated EU terrorist list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT sanctions list, and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance national terrorist list. PEP classification follows Article 1(3) of the AML Law (heads of state, ministers, supreme-court judges, ambassadors, high-ranking armed-forces officers, senior SOE directors, senior party officials, and their family members/close associates). Politically exposed persons acting in a Luxembourg or EU public capacity require enhanced due diligence (EDD) regardless of ownership percentage, supplemented by source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; ownership wires crossing a 25% threshold trigger re-verification and a fresh UBO declaration to the RBE. Any sanctions hit is a binary refusal trigger for the engagement and must be escalated to the Luxembourg FIU (CRF) for suspicious transaction reporting within 24 hours when funds are blocked.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.synopsis: The SCSp is fiscally transparent and RCSL-registered without legal personality; the CAA captive authorisation nevertheless requires UBO documentation of every natural person controlling more than 25% of the partnership, the general partner (MVP) and any supervisory board member.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.additional_ubo_note: The RBE declaration is mandatory within one month of the RCSL registration; non-compliance triggers administrative fines of EUR 100 per day, capped at EUR 5,000, with criminal exposure for false declarations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), electronic legal-filing portal at www.lbr.lu, facilitated via guichet.lu and accredited 'bureaux agréés'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in French, German or Luxembourgish using Latin-script characters; transliterations of foreign names require a French certified translation. The name must be distinctive and not misleading as to corporate form; the suffix 'Société en commandite spéciale' or 'SCSp' is mandatory. Names in non-Latin scripts (Chinese, Cyrillic, Greek) are not admitted on the RCSL record; a purely transliterated equivalent must also be provided for publication in the RESA.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.sensitive_token_authorization: Use of reassurance/insurance tokens requires a PRIOR non-objection letter from the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) or confirmation that the captive-reinsurance licence application is pending before the CAA; banking and fund tokens require prior CSSF approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCSL refusal, the applicant may (i) submit a revised name online with a written justification within 5 business days; (ii) if refusal is maintained, address a reasoned objection to the RCSL Chief Registrar within 15 days, forwarded to the Ministry of Justice for advice; (iii) within 3 months of the final administrative decision, file a judicial annulment action with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) — the appeal suspends further incorporation but does not block a parallel amended filing. In practice, counsel remedies 95% of refusals by appending a distinctive corporate identifier (e.g., 'SCSp Team Name Re') and re-submitting.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_mandate_detail: The registered office of an SCSp must be situated in Luxembourg (Law of 10 August 1915, Article 902; Law of 7 December 2016, Articles 325 and 327). The CAA requires, for captive reinsurance undertakings, the registered office to coincide with the place of effective management and the maintenance of full books and records in Luxembourg, including board-meeting minutes, underwriting files and risk-management documents.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a CAA-licensed captive reinsurer. A virtual office or a mere postal address without a physical operational footprint is rejected by the CAA and impairs Bank of Luxembourg account opening. The use of a Luxembourg professional domiciliation company (regulated by the CSSF) is acceptable as a registered-office services provider, provided the inside decision-making functions and up-to-date accounting substance remain physically in Luxembourg and demonstrable. A separate sub-filing cabinet arrangement is prohibited for licensed entities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35-50% probability per annum during the first 3 years following CAA authorisation; CAA exercises statutory on-site inspection rights under the Law of 7 December 2016, Article 71, and will generally visit the registered office within 12 months post-licence for a substance and AML review. The absence of physical infrastructure — including presence of the managing general partner or a Luxembourg-appointed management company — materially raises inspection and licence-revocation risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.substance_nexus: The SCSp must demonstrate at least the following commercial substance: a resident general partner (SCS/SCSp). if the general partner is a Luxembourg company, it must hold tangible premises; employee or outsourced actuary service in Luxembourg (external actuarial function under Solvency principles); local bank account in EUR/USD; regular board/partner meetings in Luxembourg minuted locally; all decision documents executed in Luxembourg.

stage_1.attestation: This Stage 1 dossier is prepared exclusively for pre-incorporation due diligence of an LU SCSp captive reinsurance entity. All legal citations, fees and institutional names are stated as at the date of analysis and remain subject to change upon enactment of amendments to the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, the Law of 12 November 2004, the Law of 13 January 2019 and the Law of 7 December 2016. Professional advice from a Luxembourg Avocat à la Cour and a licensed notary must be obtained prior to signing any constitutive instrument.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 17-1 to 17-28 (Special Limited Partnership or SCSp); Law of 23 July 2016 on the SCSp; amended Law of 7 December 2016 on the insurance and reinsurance sector
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS electronic declaration of incorporation (déclaration en vue de l'immatriculation au RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital is imposed for an SCSp; no escrow or bank capital deposit requirement is triggered under Luxembourg partnership law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (adopted by the Corporate General Partner of the SCSp). WHEREAS the SCSp does not have a board, the corporate general partner resolves: (1) The subscriptions to partnership interests in the register of partners are approved and each founder's contribution is recorded; (2) The registered office is fixed at [Address], Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed General Partner and [Name] Registrar; (4) All filings with the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax authorities and the Commissariat aux Assurances are authorized; (5) The General Partner may open bank accounts, execute reinsurance contracts and perform all acts for the captive reinsurance business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and reserved corporate name verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online name-check portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the SCSp in the LBR/RCS electronic interface, specifying the intended corporate name, the corporate general partner, and the proposed registered office. Verification is done against existing trade names and legal entity registrations.
required_dossiers: Completed RCS name reservation form
Identification documentation of the founding general and limited partners
Proof of address of the proposed registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, file a revised name application with the RCS name unit or appeal the refusal through the RCS review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or private practitioner; no statutory notarization required for non-in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership deed (convention de société) containing the SCSp's name, registered office address, duration, object, capital structure, general partner identity, limited partner contributions, profit-sharing rules, and governance provisions. The founding partners execute the deed in private writing unless in-kind contributions include real estate, in which case a notarial instrument is required.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Identification of the corporate general partner and its managers
Identification of the limited partners
Consent of the registered office owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or notary identifies legal or formal defects, amend and re-execute the deed with the required corrections before filing with the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership agreement and incorporation declaration electronically through the LBR/RCS e-filing platform. Pay the applicable registration fee and submit the supporting dossiers. The RCS will verify legal form, name, registered office, and general partner designation before issuing the RCS registration extract.
required_dossiers: Executed SCSp partnership agreement
Completed RCS incorporation declaration form
Certified copy of the corporate general partner's articles and board resolution
Identification documents of the partners and managers
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, cure the request within fifteen calendar days by providing the missing documentation or correcting the filing; a second rejection can be cured by resubmitting a fully compliant declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration for tax, VAT, and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply, through the RCS registration receipt or the MyGuichet.lu portal, for a Luxembourg VAT number, corporate direct tax registration, commercial permit identification, and employer accounting number if staff are to be hired. Provide the RCS extract and the partnership deed in working order.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
SCSp partnership agreement
Description of captive reinsurance activities
Identification of partners and authorized signatories
Bank details for VAT and tax refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax administration rejects or queries the application, supplement the file with a detailed business plan and corrected partner information through the MyGuichet.lu messaging facility.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and workplace authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry and Commerce, via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for the business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) required for professional services and office-based operations. The SCSp must demonstrate professional integrity and business capability of its managers, along with compliance with zoning and premises rules.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Establishment permit application form
Criminal record extracts of the general partner's managers
Evidence of professional qualifications or integrity requirements
Lease contract or ownership deed for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is queried, respond to the Ministry's clarification notice with amended documents; an outright refusal can be appealed before the Luxembourg administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Captive reinsurance licence application with the Commissariat aux Assurances
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal licence application to the CAA for authorization as a captive reinsurance undertaking under the amended Law of 7 December 2016 on the insurance and reinsurance sector. The application must include the scheme of operations, proof of own funds, technical reserve policy, corporate governance structure, and the roles of the general partner and registrar.
required_dossiers: CAA licence application form
SCSp partnership deed and RCS extract
Programme of operations for captive reinsurance
Evidence of own funds and financial soundness
Technical reserve valuation methodology
Fitness and propriety declarations for directors and managers
Audited financial statements of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On refusal or query, provide additional justification, modify the governance structure, or file an administrative appeal to the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of the notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) – Luxembourg insurance and reinsurance supervisory authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Captive Reinsurance Undertaking Authorization (Agrément en tant qu'entreprise de réassurance captive)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report for pure office/administrative captive reinsurance premises; simplified environmental notification or administrative zoning checklist with the local commune is required before occupancy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process discharges; sanitary wastewater must comply with the municipal wastewater discharge regulations of the commune and with grand-ducal wastewater standards; office heating emissions limited to those of standard commercial boiler installations with VOC thresholds under EU solvent emissions legislation; any waste, including electronic equipment and recovered paper, must be handled by an authorized waste collector and documented under Luxembourg waste management law

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from the communal fire prevention authority and the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for the registered office; structural load and building occupancy clearance is obtained through the local commune's building permit procedure; occupational safety and health compliance is inspected and cleared by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including workplace ergonomic, workstation, and emergency exit requirements

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue; VAT administration: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); official government portal: https://guichet.lu; electronic tax filing portal: https://espace.public.lu; corporate registry: Registre de commerce et des sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg SCSp must first file the partnership agreement and incorporation documents with the RCS. Upon RCS registration, the ACD automatically assigns a Luxembourg national tax identification number for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes. The SCSp must separately apply to the AEDT for a VAT identification number whenever it will carry on a taxable economic activity in Luxembourg and does not qualify for the small-business turnover exemption. Non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment may need to register directly with the ACD, usually through a Luxembourg accredited tax agent, to obtain a local TIN for withholding tax and fiscal transparency reporting. Foreign legal persons that are not otherwise required to register may obtain a TIN by submitting a formal request to the ACD with notarised constitutional documents, proof of identity of managers/partners, and evidence of a Luxembourg registered office or tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory construction and cannot elect to be taxed at entity level. LuxSA, Lux S.à r.l., and other corporate vehicles can opt into the Luxembourg fiscal consolidation regime (intégration fiscale) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax where a 95% shareholding is held by a fully taxable resident parent; transparent partnerships cannot be the consolidating parent. The SCSp may, however, elect VAT grouping membership as part of an assujetti unique group if strong financial, economic, and organisational integration exists. Taxpayers may also apply to the ACD for a formal advance tax ruling confirming the transparency treatment or the absence of a permanent establishment. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD/MLI can override partnership transparency if the structure is used to achieve double non-taxation; no elective exception is permitted for that outcome.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA), implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) for small businesses established in Luxembourg; non-established taxable persons have no registration threshold if they make taxable supplies subject to Luxembourg VAT or import goods; cross-border insurance/reinsurance services are generally VAT-exempt under Article 135(1)(a) of the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate real-time tax clearance, mandatory e-invoicing API filing, or digital stamping for general B2B invoices. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all invoices issued to public-sector contracting entities via the PEPPOL-bilingual format under the Luxembourg e-invoicing regime. For all other transactions, taxpayers may issue paper or EDI invoices, but must preserve transaction-level audit files for VAT verification. Insurance and reinsurance premiums, claims, and commissions are VAT-exempt without an electronic-invoice clearance duty; however, invoices must still be issued to policyholders and contain the statutory VAT-exemption reference.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Luxembourg-resident seller may zero-rate the supply of goods exported from the EU if the goods are physically dispatched or transported to a non-EU destination and the exporter retains adequate documentary evidence within the statutory time limits. Services consisting of the provision of insurance or reinsurance, including captive reinsurance underwriting, are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT when supplied to a non-EU business customer, or VAT-exempt in the EU context; they do not attract a 0% rate. For mixed export and non-export transactions, VAT input credits are restricted to the proportion attributable to taxable transactions unless the special insurance/reinsurance exemption (which disallows input deduction) applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Luxembourg/EU Single Administrative Document - ECS status confirmation containing MRN)
Bill of Lading or other transport document evidencing physical movement out of the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/SWIFT record proving the export sale proceeds are credited to a Luxembourg bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties_pl: The above placeholder keys are not part of the mandated schema and must be deleted. The actual field has been placed at root level below.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for prudential and AML/CFT supervision
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member with full capital account and current account convertibility under EU treaty freedoms (TFEU Art. 63) and domestic law. SCSp vehicles may freely convert, remit, and repatriate profits, premiums, claims, and investment proceeds in any currency, subject to EU sanctions, AML/KYC verification, FATCA/CRS reporting, and the substance/anti-abuse rules applied by the Luxembourg tax authorities. No exchange control licensing, surrender, or central bank approval is required for captive reinsurance premium remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg does not impose mandatory export proceeds surrender, conversion quotas, or repatriation timelines. All distributions, dividends, and insurance-related proceeds from an SCSp account may be transferred abroad without central bank filing, except where a wire crosses a sanctioned jurisdiction or a payment institution requires a specific EU payment purpose code for statistical balance of payments reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited viability. Luxembourg-regulated EMI/payment institution licenses (under CSSF) may be used for EUR collection of small premium payments or Treasury sub-accounts, but an SCSp captive reinsurance vehicle should maintain its primary settlement and reserve accounts at a full-scope credit institution to ensure SWIFT clearing, segregated client money treatment, FATCA/CRS golden-source reporting, and buy-side acceptance by licensed reinsurers. Non-EU/EEA offshore digital EMIs are not viable primary rails because they lack Luxembourg banking licence status, acceptable correspondent clearing relationships, and the ability to hold multi-currency premium reserves in segregated low-risk accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes, a physical KYC interview is effectively mandatory at Luxembourg Tier-1 banks. The general partner (Gérant) or an authorized senior executive with actual management authority must appear in person at the bank’s Luxembourg office; remote video onboarding is accepted only for pre-existing clients and only as a supplementary measure. New SCSp SPVs with non-resident UBOs will require at least one in-person board or bank meeting in Luxembourg, supported by a registered Luxembourg address and substance documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex UBO chain with multiple intermediate holding entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart, notarized passport copies of UBOs, UBO register extract (RBE), partnership agreement (SCSp agreement), certificate of good standing, and consolidated proof of source of wealth for all ultimate principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reinsurance premium flows classified as unexplained round-tripping or disguised capital recycling
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed fronting/captive reinsurance treaty, actuarial premium certificate, loss reserve valuation report, intercompany transfer pricing documentation (OECD Level 3 report), and board minutes confirming genuine insurance risk assumption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregulated captive SPV with unclear insurance license status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from a Luxembourg Avocat à la Cour confirming the captive is exempt or falling outside licensed insurance business; confirmation from Commissariat aux Assurances; and CSSF classification letter if required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Named sanctions or adverse media hits on non-resident UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions screening report (Refinitiv/Dow Jones), negative news search, UBO passports, proof of termination of any debarred relationships, and a remedial compliance undertaking signed by all directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance relative to bank management and decision-making
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg office lease, payroll records for local substance, minutes of board meetings held in Luxembourg, service agreements with local administrator (if any), proof of authority given to Luxembourg-domiciled general partner, and a detailed substance dossier for the Luxembourg tax administration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital and premium injections are effected through SWIFT MT103 or MT202/MT102 batch transfers, crediting a dedicated EUR or USD IBAN. Each wire must clearly reference the reinsurance treaty number and a validated payment purpose code: for equity contributions use 'CAPC' or ISO 20022 'CAPC'; for premium income use 'INSA' (Insurance Premium) or 'REINS' (Reinsurance Premium) unless the bank specifies '13000' under ECB BPM6 balance-of-payments codification; for intercompany loans or funding use 'INTS' or 'LOAN'. For contributions exceeding EUR 30,000, the bank will require source-of-funds declarations, underlying capital call or policy documents, and sanctions verification before making funds available.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound indemnity claims and premium ceding are executed via SWIFT MT103 (single) or MT102 (bulk) with purpose code 'INSA' or 'REINS' and a policy/claims reference. Larger reserve-backed transfers may use TARGET2 for EUR and SWIFT correspondent through the bank’s clearing network for USD/GBP/CHF. For irrevocable trade settlements, commercial documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) or standby LCs (ISP 98) can be issued by the Tier-1 Luxembourg bank to support the group's captive insurance collateral obligations; internal treasury sweeps to ultimate parent accounts use MT101/MT102 with 'INTC' and evidence of arm's-length intercompany settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (FXA) with Luxembourg/EU bank counterparties under ISDA 2002 or local FX master agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, KRW) for premium flows originating from operating subsidiaries outside the EU
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) to manage long-term reinsurance reserve liabilities in a different currency
FX swaps (tom-next/spot-next) for short-term liquidity management and premium funding alignment
Currency options (FXO) on a limited notional basis for hedging adverse FX moves in reserve-linked claim exposures, subject to the SCSp’s treasury policy and CSSF derivative eligibility
Commodity and index-linked derivatives are not permissible unless directly hedging captive policy risk; generic speculative derivatives are excluded by corporate treasury mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS annual data confirmation (annual return) updating registered office, general partner, managers, and professional domiciliation data of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of RCS registration; immediately upon any change in registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS may issue a formal query, levy administrative fines, and eventually strike the SCSp from the register if the annual data confirmation remains outstanding for more than 12 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Luxembourg GAAP) and, if applicable, management and auditor's report of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the SCSp's governing bodies no later than six months after the financial year-end; RCS deposit within one month after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-deposit is punishable by fines of EUR 1,500 to EUR 10,000; persistent failure can lead to mandatory strike-off, court-ordered publication, and disqualification-type measures against the general partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership annual confirmation and RBE update on partnership-interest transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within one month after the RBE registration anniversary; transfer-driven RBE updates within one month after any SCSp interest transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML administrative fines and criminal penalties for inaccurate, missing, or stale declarations; the RBE register may be blocked, and the CAA or criminal authorities may impose sanctions under the Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CAA supervisory and prudential package for the licensed captive reinsurance SCSp (annual accounts, statutory auditor's report, actuary report, Solvency II own-risk and solvency assessment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts filed with the RCS and the CAA within six months of the financial year-end; Solvency II quantitative and narrative reports typically due by 31 March of the following year, and the ORSA or RSR by 30 April unless a CAA-approved extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAA may impose periodic penalty payments, suspend or revoke the captive reinsurance authorisation, and forward findings to the public prosecutor; non-filing also exposes the general partner to personal civil liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit is required if the SCSp exceeds any two of the following Luxembourg size thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. In addition, a licensed captive reinsurance undertaking must appoint a CAA-approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) regardless of size, and must also engage an actuary for the annual report.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and the Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; Solvency II valuation rules apply to the CAA prudential returns; IFRS is not mandatory for stand-alone statutory accounts of an SCSp unless elected for consolidated group purposes and accepted by the general partners.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp's annual confirmation protocol requires reconciliation of the RBE record to the register of partners and the latest assignment deeds. Any transfer of a partnership interest or change in beneficial ownership must be lodged with the RBE within one month of the transaction. The annual confirmation is a zero-fee declaration made on the RBE anniversary date confirming that the recorded beneficial ownership remains accurate; where no change occurred, the register and RBE are aligned before the confirmation is filed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partnership-Interest Transfers and Assignments
Register of General Partner, Managers and Authorized Representatives
Minutes of Partners' Meetings and General Partner Resolutions
Statutory Accounting Books and Source Documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$5,500–US$11,000 (EUR 5,000–10,000) for a Luxembourg licensed domiciliation agent providing SCSp registered office, AML/KYC, and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$9,000–US$25,000 (EUR 8,000–22,500) for a small captive reinsurance SCSp, including the CAA-required certified audit and actuarial certificate

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined corporate income tax 17%, solidarity surcharge 7% on CIT, and municipal business tax average 6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays; preferential IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income) and investment tax credits (e.g., 8% for digitalisation) available; SCSp is fiscally transparent, so income is taxed at partner level unless election to be taxable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Corporate Income Tax Return) for taxable entities; SCSp files Form 301 (Partnership Information Return) via MyGuichet.lu or eTVA electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 31 December upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For SCSp, report the partnership's total income; non-resident partners must attach their share allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (including reinsurance reserves and technical provisions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure arm's length pricing for related-party reinsurance premiums; maintain TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credit, investment credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim credits via their home jurisdiction; Luxembourg return is informational.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of EUR 250 to EUR 2,500; daily surcharge of 0.1% on unpaid tax for each month of delay, plus interest at 0.6% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 12 months; treaty rates may apply)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the partner's jurisdiction and Form 22 (withholding tax exemption request) to the Luxembourg tax authorities (ACD) before or at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15%, reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive (if beneficial owner and ≥25% shareholding); Interest: statutory 15%, reduced to 0% under EU directive or treaty (e.g., 0% with most OECD countries).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000; Master File required if group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies substance requirements under anti-abuse rules (e.g., ATAD, GAAR) and for tax residency; captive reinsurance must demonstrate real economic activity: local staff, office, decision-making, and risk management functions. Failure to meet substance may lead to recharacterisation and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of reinsurance premiums or artificial shifting of profits to low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to EUR 250,000 or 200% of evaded tax; criminal prosecution for directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for civil restitution; travel bans and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp used as a conduit without real staff, office, or risk management; no active underwriting or claims handling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits; reclassification as a taxable entity; penalty of EUR 10,000 to EUR 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable for unpaid taxes and penalties; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence on reinsurance counterparties or suspicious transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; license revocation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for AML breaches; imprisonment up to 5 years and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing on related-party reinsurance contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income; penalty of 10% of the adjustment amount; daily fines for non-documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; civil restitution.
